NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
The maintainer's active-development policy (`CLAUDE.md:5`) makes CLI determinism serve current project state, active changes and implementation, and the bundle being closed; older archives are passive historical evidence for LLM interpretation, preserved byte-for-byte but not parsed or re-executed as current input. The withdrawn compatibility campaign (`docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/grace-implementation-queue.md:154-156`) is replaced by small governed removals of the remaining archive dependencies, of which this is the first.
Three automatic readers currently open archived XML: the archive branch of `validateChangeBundlesInDirectory` in `src/artifact/grammar.ts`; the archived-plan assertion loop in `src/lint/core.ts`; and the active-plus-archive operational validation in `src/query/core.ts` that feeds `loadGraceArtifactIndex`. The boundary is drawn at automatic validation and query-index inputs. The explicit `--as <status>` preview is deliberately **inside**: `src/lint/core.ts:134-136` computes the validator location from the requested virtual status, so `--as applied` can validate a selected current/active artifact under archive-status rules. That is a current-artifact check, not an old-archive reader, and the shared single-artifact `validateChangeArtifact` (`src/artifact/grammar.ts:678`) therefore stays intact. Retirement of explicit archived selection belongs to its own consumer slice.
Why remove reads rather than suppress diagnostics: suppressing an error after parsing still reads the historical bytes, still couples current results to historical format drift, and still pays the parse cost. The proof is therefore a read-boundary observation — a `bun:test` `spyOn` over the real exported `readGraceXmlArtifact`, calling through to the original, showing zero archive-path calls and a positive current-artifact call for each of `validateNgraceProject`, `lintGraceProject`, and `loadGraceArtifactIndex` — plus real-CLI clean/mutate/restored behaviour. Why not disable the validators: active, selected-current, graph, verification, identity, and preview checks must keep refusing, and this bundle keeps them, so a disabled validator cannot pass as an opaque archive.
Two archived-bundle rules are overturned. The unrelated-malformed-archive refusal preserved by `C-ARCHIVE-CORPUS-BASELINE-2-D5F2E1C3` was the counterweight to excluding `.ngrace` scratch code from implementation-source collection; the exclusion and every guard survive, so the counterweight is answered by a current-only rather than a whole-corpus validator. The archived spec-to-plan coverage rule at `src/artifact/grammar.ts:1474-1477` ("Run for active and archive: historical bundles that already match stay quiet; mismatches surface so archives remain truthful"; G-05 / Safeguard 5) is retired for archives because current schemas validate current work and the current close; old evidence is retained without retroactive conformance enforcement. Active coverage stays. This is not `C-GRAPH-COVERAGE`'s different GraphAnchors/OWS archive policy.
Automatic current validation and navigation, with the explicit preview preserved:
Sequence: automatic paths read only current artifacts; preview stays

Alternatives.Alternative: Suppress archive-derived diagnostics after reading them (filter issues whose file is under `.ngrace/changes/archive/`). Rejected: it keeps parsing historical bytes, keeps current results coupled to historical format drift, and hides rather than removes the dependency; its output-only checks would also pass a parsing-and-discarding implementation.

Keep parsing but ignore results, treating the archive as a best-effort reader. Rejected for the same reason plus cost: a malformed archive still allocates parse work and can still throw on a path that is not guarded, so the boundary is not enforceable.

Remove archive contents from the automatic validation and query-index inputs, keeping directory-name identity checks, active and selected-current refusals, active coverage, projections, exclusions, the explicit preview, and byte preservation. Chosen: it matches the policy and is provable with a read-boundary observation plus paired clean/red/restored controls.

Also change the explicit `--as` preview or the shared single-artifact validator. Rejected: a current `--as applied` preview validates a selected current artifact under archive-status rules (`src/lint/core.ts:134-136`) and is not an old-archive reader; changing it would break a current capability this slice must keep.

Stop validating archive directories at all, including names. Rejected: it would silently disarm the identity checks and the missing-change-directory guard, turning the boundary into a disabled validator.

Change the whole lifecycle, including apply/close, status, scope, navigation, and reporting, in one bundle. Rejected as oversized and not independently verifiable; the maintainer sanctioned a first small slice with the rest in dependent bundles.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Status and scope attribution over archived applied changes: `collectAppliedChangeScopes` in `src/artifact/scope.ts` and the status surface in `src/grace-status.ts` still name archives. Owner: a separate dependent bundle; not changed here. Its outputs may inherit the shared validator's new current-only behaviour, which is expected, not a promised diagnostic set.

Explicit archived navigation and archived measurement modes: `src/query/change.ts` resolves an archive location by name, and `src/grace-context.ts` models an archived-sibling slice and an archived-measurement-only subject. Owner: separate dependent bundles; the runtime `src/grace-context.ts` is unchanged here and no compatibility test is authored for it.

Historical reporting and post-archive verdict evaluation: `src/calibration/report.ts`, `src/review/outcomes.ts`, and `src/review/core.ts` read archives for their own reports and verdicts. Owner: separate dependent bundles.

The current-close transaction: deterministically verify the selected new record and then treat it as history. This bundle does not change `ngrace apply`, `ngrace supersede`, or the close. Owner: the current-close boundary bundle.

User-facing current-only teaching and release documentation. `README.md` and `examples/` are unchanged here; the full cutover depends on removing the remaining archive consumers. Owner: the final cutover bundle.

Scenario.Title: Read boundary: zero archive calls, positive current control
Scenario.Steps: In each in-scope unit test, install a `bun:test` `spyOn` over the real exported `readGraceXmlArtifact` that calls through to the original and records each `file` argument. Drive the real `validateNgraceProject`, `lintGraceProject`, or `loadGraceArtifactIndex` over a complete ordinary project with one opaque unrelated archive bundle. Assert the recorded set contains no path under `.ngrace/changes/archive/` and does contain at least one current-artifact path. Restore the spy. No fake parser and no fabricated return is used, so a parsing-and-discarding implementation cannot pass.

Scenario.Title: Isolated archive mutations do not move current output
Scenario.Steps: Build a complete ordinary throwaway project; capture clean lint JSON, `module find M-QUERY` output, and the selected-active context slice bytes. Apply one archive change at a time and restore it exactly before the next: malformed `spec.xml`; malformed `plan.xml`; a differing `graceVersion`; a missing required section; an invalid `design-context.xml` companion. Each case yields 0 errors and exit 0, module navigation returns the same record, and the selected-active slice is unchanged. Context and module output compare byte-for-byte; lint JSON omits only the documented `generatedAt` field, and that normalization is disclosed. No other field is filtered.

Scenario.Title: Active, projection, and preview corruption still refuse
Scenario.Steps: On the same throwaway project, plant in turn malformed active governance XML, a version-invalid active spec, a required-section-invalid active plan, an invalid active assertion, corrupted graph or verification projection, selected active-change corruption, and corruption of the selected current plan under `--as applied --assertions current`. Each exits non-zero with a discriminating code and, on exact restoration, recovers the byte-identical green output. The preview recovers the same plan hash and the same JSON after omitting only `generatedAt`. This proves the archive boundary did not disable a validator.

Scenario.Title: Only names are read under the archive
Scenario.Steps: Rename an archive bundle directory to a non-`C-*` name: `change.invalid-bundle-id` still fires. Add a loose `.xml` file directly under the archive directory: `change.unexpected-file` still fires. Neither check opens the file. Removing the archive directory still makes `project.missing-change-directory` fire.

Scenario.Title: Active coverage stays; archived coverage retires
Scenario.Steps: An active approved spec/plan pair whose plan DurableScope covers a different module than the spec AffectedAreas still yields `change.scope-does-not-cover-spec` and `change.plan-scope-exceeds-spec`. The same mismatch already archived is no longer a current issue, because current schemas validate current work and the current close, not historical conformance. This is the archived spec-to-plan coverage rule at `src/artifact/grammar.ts:1474-1477` (G-05 / Safeguard 5), distinct from `C-GRAPH-COVERAGE`'s GraphAnchors/OWS archive policy.
